text.p: Sterling stabilised after a week of rapid gains, settling around 2.44 marks in the European morning.

Dealers and analysts said higher oil prices and healthy stock prices were likely to underpin the stronger pound, although short-term profit-taking would chip away at any further attempts to head north.

"With little expected in the way of news today, sterling is likely to tread water," said a UK bank dealer. "I can't see any major swing today, and the pace of recent gains is certainly not likely to continue."

At 0900 GMT, the pound was trading at 2.4419/24 marks against 2.4375/80 late Wednesday. Cable, which has been plotting a calmer path than stg/mark in recent days, was firmer at $1.5863/73 against $1.5830/35.
Sterling's trade weighted index was at 88.8 against yesterday's close of 88.7.
"Firmer oil prices are not doing sterling any harm, and stock prices are firm. Sterling has also been undervalued," said Ian Amstad, economist at Bankers Trust.
Chart analysts said sterling/mark was set for some sideways consolidation before returning to the upside.
They plotted support at 2.4310 marks, which they said was the site of a five-day exponential moving average and a sturdy prop last night.

Nick Shamin, currency analyst at Technical Data in London, said resistance around 2.4385 marks lay ahead of 2.4500, a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the drop from 2.6235 hit in January 1994 to the record low of 2.1683 seen last November.
